entry.title: A turn for the child using it, and help waiting
entry.summary: Davies’s home approach gives a child time with an activity and supports the child who wants the next turn. Public places may call for a shorter ending so others can have a turn.
entry.cue: One child is using something another child wants.
detail: At home, she allows repetition rather than requiring a child to hand over the activity immediately. Watch whether another child’s company is welcome, offer simple words for each child’s wish, and step in to stop pushing or grabbing.
The waiting child needs support too. At a shared playground, Davies instead acknowledges the person waiting and gives the current turn a clear ending as a courtesy.
Before visitors arrive, she suggests letting a child put away especially important toys and agreeing that guests may use what remains.

ageContext.bookAge: Davies describes mainly parallel play before 2½ and possible interest in playing together around 2½.

ageContext.note: Watch whether company is welcome; the ages do not require a child to share or play together.

displayContext.footer: You don’t need a different home. Start with what you have.
